newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel says weak euro not answer to jobless queues.
newsitem.headline: Waigel says weak euro not answer to jobless queues.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Tuesday at an international monetary conference that depreciation of the euro should not be used as a means to combat unemployment.
He told the Global 24 monetary conference: "The exchange rate of the euro should not be used as a tool to foster employment".
The European Monetary Union conference, called Global 24, links participants across the globe with a video link-up.
Waigel also said Germany intended to meet the criteria for entry to EMU in the short and long term, adding that there could be no automatic entry to the currency union for any country.
"Germany will do everything to meet the criteria now and forever," he said in a panel discussion. "There can be no automatic entry for any country to EMU and no automatic exclusions".

"Convergence is more important than the timetable for every country," Waigel said, referring to the fact that meeting economic criteria set out for entry to monetary union should take precedence over the planned launch date in 1999.

Countering suggestions from some countries, such as France, that a cooperation group between finance ministers of countries could act as a counter-party to the future European Central Bank, Waigel said this would not be the case.
Germany like other nations is currently having difficulties meeting the convergence criteria, struggling both with a high budget deficit and a high debt ratio.
The Maastricht Treaty states that countries must meet targets on these fiscal criteria as well as on interest rates, exchange rates and inflation.
